issues.legal_issue: An earlier interim order does not prevent a different decision at the final stage when the decision is based on evidence or a factual position clarified later.
material_facts: An application to discontinue the possession proceedings had earlier been rejected before evidence or statements were recorded, on the understanding that the civil suit concerned different property.
Later statements established that the civil suit and the possession proceedings concerned the same property, and that the civil court had ordered the parties to maintain the status quo.
issues.conclusion: The earlier interim orders did not bind the Magistrate or prevent reconsideration on the later record, and the High Court erred in treating them as final and binding.
issues.legal_principle: Interim orders, even if confirmed by a higher court, do not prevent a contrary order at the final hearing. The decision applies this settled principle to the proceedings under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the High Court’s exercise of power under Section 482.

predicates.final_stage_after_interim_order: A decision is being made at a later, final stage after an earlier interim order in the same proceeding.
predicates.later_evidence_clarifies_material_facts: Evidence or statements recorded later clarify material facts that were previously understood differently.

issues.definition: When a later final-stage decision follows an interim order and later evidence clarifies material facts, the earlier interim order does not prevent reconsideration.

issues.legal_issue: Possession proceedings should not continue in parallel with a pending civil suit concerning possession or title to the same property when the civil court can grant protective relief concerning that property.
material_facts: A civil suit seeking relief concerning title and possession of the property was filed before the possession proceedings began.
The civil court had ordered the parties to maintain the status quo and could grant further protection concerning the property.
The parties’ statements established that both proceedings concerned the same property, and the possession proceedings had not resulted in a final order.
The Magistrate discontinued the possession proceedings because the civil court was already dealing with the matter and had granted protective relief.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate was right to discontinue the possession proceedings, and the High Court’s order requiring them to resume was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, parallel possession proceedings should not continue when a civil suit concerns possession or declaration of title to the same property and the civil court can grant relief protecting it. The Court applied Ram Sumer Puri Mahant v. State of U.P. and distinguished Jhummamal alias Devandas v. State of Madhya Pradesh, which concerned a civil suit filed after a final order in the possession proceedings. The principle avoids multiplicity of litigation and recognizes that civil court orders bind the Magistrate on the matter before it.

rule.if: parallel_possession_proceeding and pending_civil_property_suit and same_property_in_both_proceedings and civil_suit_concerns_possession_or_title and civil_court_can_protect_property and no_final_possession_order

predicates.parallel_possession_proceeding: A summary proceeding to determine possession is underway while a civil property suit is pending.
predicates.pending_civil_property_suit: A civil suit concerning the property is pending.
predicates.same_property_in_both_proceedings: The civil suit and the possession proceeding concern the same property.
predicates.civil_suit_concerns_possession_or_title: The civil suit seeks a determination concerning possession or title to the property.
predicates.civil_court_can_protect_property: The civil court can grant relief protecting the property while the suit is pending.
predicates.no_final_possession_order: The possession proceeding has not resulted in a final order.

issues.definition: When a pending possession proceeding concerns the same property as a civil suit about possession or title, the civil court can protect the property, and no final possession order has been made, the parallel possession proceeding should be discontinued.

issues.legal_issue: A higher court should not impose strictures on a lower court merely because it takes a different view where the lower court adopted a possible view.
material_facts: The Magistrate discontinued the possession proceedings after finding that the civil court was dealing with the same property and had ordered the parties to maintain the status quo.
The High Court disagreed with the Magistrate and made strictures against the Magistrate.
issues.conclusion: The strictures were uncalled for; a different view by the High Court was not, by itself, a ground for making them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that two views may be possible and that a higher court’s disagreement with the lower court’s view alone does not justify strictures against it.

predicates.higher_court_reviews_lower_court_decisio: A higher court reviews a decision made by a lower court.
predicates.lower_court_adopted_a_possible_view: The lower court adopted a view that was reasonably open on the matter before it.
predicates.strictures_rest_only_on_disagreement: The higher court’s strictures are based only on its disagreement with the lower court’s view.

issues.definition: When a higher court reviews a lower court that adopted a possible view, strictures based only on disagreement with that view are unwarranted.
